newsitem.title: KENYA: Iran pledges to back Kenyan development.
newsitem.headline: Iran pledges to back Kenyan development.

text.p: Iran offered on Thursday to throw its weight behind Kenya's energy, industry and farm sectors by installing power stations, building storage facilities for liquefied petroleum gas and repairing roads.

In a joint memorandum of understanding signed by Kenyan Foreign Minister Kalonzo Musyoka and Iranian Commerce Minister Yahya Al-Eshaq, Iran also offered to help train Kenyans and open avenues for trade in Iran and the Gulf region
The memorandum was signed at the end of a four-day tour of Kenya by Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani and a technical working group meeting of senior Iranian and Kenyan officials.
Rafsanjani is also visiting Uganda, South Africa, Zimbabwe, Tanzania and Sudan to drum up business for Iran.

The memorandum said Kenya and Iran agreed to boost bilateral cooperation and trade -- with Kenya considering reduction of customs tariffs for Iranian handmade carpets and handicrafts -- and expanding relationships between Kenyan and Iranian banks.
"The Iranian side expressed its willingness to cooperate in construction of liquefied petroleum gas storage and distribution facilities, and to supply the gas," the memorandum said.

"Iran expressed its readiness to provide technical services and finance rehabilitation of the Mombasa oil refinery; and readiness to consider training Kenyan geologists and engineers," the memorandum added.

"The National Iran Oil Company is ready to consider the crude oil requirements of Kenya under conditions of the international oil market and establishment of a letter of credit confirmed through one of the banks acceptable to it," it added.

Kenya currently imports about 15 percent of its annual crude oil needs of 2.2 million tonnes from Iran, according to a Kenyan government official. He said Mombasa handled 8 million tonnes of cargo per year but had the capacity to take up to 20 million.

The memorandum said Iran was ready to provide equipment and services, design, installation, maintenance and training of manpower for dams, power plants and stations, installation of refinery, petrochemical projects and power transmission lines.
"The Kenya side would identify the areas of cooperation and would inform the Iran side," the memorandum said.
The memorandum said the Technical Company of Iran was ready to implement small-size pipe manufacturing and composite projects in Nairobi and negotaitions on this would begin soon.
Iran said it would supply equipment and engineering services to expand Kenya's electricity and water supplies.

"The Iranian side announced its readiness to cooperate with Kenya in providing technical services for installation of units such as plastic and melamine manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, syringes, furniture and wooded articles and foor processing industries among others," the memorandum said.

It said Iran also planned to help Kenya in research for pyrethrum development, building of earth dams and watershed management projects. It wanted to export to Kenya surplus of production of nitrogen and urea fertilisers, it added.
Iran offered assist Kenya to establish projects, extension, renovation and modification of existing cement plants, build rural access roads and provide technology in bee-keeping.
Other areas of cooperation in the momorandum were fisheries, mining of metals, environment, health, tourism, transport and communication, culture, education and free trade zones.
Neither side said how much these projects might cost.
